svg.title: Scene 87: What is observable, by whom
svg.desc: Four frames fill one table: eight observers against six things that could be observed. 1, a tap and a radio listener: a card reader sees the card number of a plastic card; an NFC phone touching a tag sees only what the owner chose to show; a radio listener sees only the rotating identifier. 2, a passer-by’s phone sees the identifier, its own location and the report it seals; the relay sees a lookup hash, the sealed report and metadata, never the location. 3, the owner decrypts the location; someone who planted a tag sees exactly what an owner sees — the location of the person carrying it. 4, an organisation’s admin: unknown, it depends on what is enrolled and shared; an outside attacker without the account sees only what a radio listener sees, unless they take over the account. Unknown is marked as a finding, not left blank.
svg.text: Same tag, eight observers. Unknown is a finding,

text.tspan: * unless they take over the owner’s account (Scene 48) —
then they see what the owner sees.
● yes ○ no ≈ metadata or partial ? unknown: depends on
what an organisation enrols and shares — not involved
Tracker rows follow Apple’s documented Find My design
and agree with Scene 46 and demo D. A plastic card sends
its number; a phone wallet sends a device token instead
